thread:
incident-bot: PAGE | latency: p99 streaming stalls above SLO (eu-west2) — paging @sara (on-call) and @netops :rotating_light:

sara: on it. reading dashboards now — link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming/latency?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west2

mario: saw a short spike on p95 ~ 2m ago, but p99 sustained for ~8m, streaming tail stalls ~50-200ms extra per token. clients reporting degraded realtime streams.

liz: customer-impact: two customers flagged intermittent stalls and reconnects on chat streaming. CS notified.

kevin: quick check — is this DNS or TLS handshake increase? last time similar it was NAT ephemeral port exhaustion. running a few probes now.

netops: running `mtr` to one problematic host in eu-west2, seeing packet loss ~3-6% across a single hop (azb->azc transit).

jordan: captured tcpdump on proxy pool node-azb-3 — lots of retransmits and TLS handshake retries to remote NAT IPs. snippet:

```
14:23:01.123456 IP node-azb-3.54321 > remote-eu-nat.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, length 0
14:23:01.345678 IP node-azb-3.54321 > remote-eu-nat.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, length 0 (retry)
14:23:02.456789 IP node-azb-3.54321 > remote-eu-nat.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, length 0 (retry)
```

incident-bot: autotriage note: route-flap suspicion + NAT path congestion. recommended playbook: egress-steer or traffic-split.

sara: action plan: 1) short-term: split egress for streaming from eu-west2->eu-west1 for new requests only, keep existing connections; 2) mid-term: netops to investigate transit hop and open cloud ticket; 3) postmortem items after stability.

mario: I can push a traffic-split rule at the LB level — will do a 70/30 shift to eu-west1 for streaming-route group. applying canary now. command:`/infra/ctl route apply --group streaming-eu --split 70:30 --to eu-west1`

liz: FYI customers asked for ETA. i'm sending an interim note: "we're actively mitigating; some streams may see reconnects; engineers are routing new sessions to an alternate region."

kevin: rolling change started. watching connection churn and p99.

(2m pass)

mario: canary at 70/30 is up. new session success rate to eu-west1 looks good (200 OKs).

netops: cloud provider support ticket opened, referencing traceroute + pcap. provider reports transient fiber congestion on inter-az path and are rerouting.

jordan: after split, saw immediate drop in TLS handshake retries on the remaining eu-west2 nodes (p99 down ~65%). streaming tail stalls reduced for new sessions routed to eu-west1.

kevin: metric snapshot after 10m: p99 token latency eu-west2 old path 1.2s -> 420ms; overall p99 across eu clustering from 1.1s -> 480ms. p95 back under SLO.

incident-bot: NOTE: paging suppressed for 30m while monitoring.

sara: ok good. netops keep escalation with provider. mario keep split for 30m, then slowly return traffic when provider confirms stable or we see steady-state for 20m.

mario: will ramp back with 10% steps every 2m once provider green. logging runbook action for rollout/rollback: `/runbooks/incidents/egress-quick-split.md`

liz: customers notified with interim update. CS will keep a watch.

netops: provider confirms reroute in progress; they expect propagation in ~12 minutes. also recommended replacing a flaky NAT gateway instance in eu-west2 — we'll coordinate with infra.

kevin: planning maintenance window to replace nat-gw-5 after traffic normalized. will schedule in next 2 hours.

jordan: capturing all pcap and saving under /archive/incidents/1729998888 for postmortem. also saved streaming session ids with higher latency to help evals.

sara: closing the active pager to reduce noise; keeping thread open for updates. once provider confirms, mario please start slow rollback and post results here.

(40m later)

mario: rollback started at 1729999288 — stepping 10% per 2m. monitoring looks stable. final rollback completed at 1729999448.

netops: NAT gateway replacement completed and health checks show 0 retransmits on replaced instance. provider confirmed no further fiber congestion after reroute.

kevin: final metrics: p99 steady at 380-460ms, streaming error rate back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated.

liz: customer follow-ups queued, sending status update and summary.

sara: thanks team — will convert this to a P1 postmortem doc with timeline, root cause (provider fiber instability caused packet loss leading to TLS retries and NAT path congestion), customer impact, and action items (egress reroute runbook, NAT replacement precheck, add more cross-region traffic-split automation). assigning owners in postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — please file postmortem at https://pm.redwood.example/incidents/1729998888 and tag `networking` and `runtime`
summary: Cross-zone / NAT-induced TLS handshake spike causing p99 streaming stalls; mitigated by short-term traffic split to eu-west1 and NAT gateway replacement, provider reroute; postmortem and follow-ups scheduled.
